Different animals, different posters.
Our class made posters for an animal centre this week. At first, Leo wanted to put the youngest puppy on every poster. “It is cuter than the older dogs,” he said. Our teacher asked us to find out more about the animals before choosing. We visited the centre with an adult. The puppies ran faster than the older dogs and wanted to play all the time. The older dogs were quieter and stayed beside the visitors. One old dog, Gold, sat patiently while a little girl read to him. In the next room, a parrot had a brighter tail than the other birds. I drew it, but my first picture was not very good. Eva showed me how to draw the small stripes more carefully. My second picture was better than my first. Later, we discussed which animals should be on our posters. Leo said he had changed his mind. Gold was less active than the puppies, but he was good company for someone who liked quiet afternoons. We made different posters for different animals. I learned that a better poster does more than show a cute face. It helps people understand what an animal is like.
